div.head: Cn 1027 16
div.ab: Nunc igitur praecipio et obtestor omnes meos episcopos et regni praepositos, per fidem quam Deo et mihi debetis, quatinus faciatis ut, antequam ego Angliam veniam, omnia debita quae Deo secundum legem antiquam debemus, sint persoluta, scilicet elemosinae pro aratris et decimae animalium ipsius anni procreatorum et denarii quos Romae ad Sanctum Petrum debemus, sive ex urbibus sive ex villis, et mediante Augusto decimae frugum et in festivitate Sancti Martini primitiae seminum ad ecclesiam sub cuius parrochia quisque deget, quae Anglice ciricsceatt nominantur.

Now, therefore, I enjoin upon and beseech all you my bishops and the reeves of the kingdom, by the fealty which you owe to God and to me, to bring it to pass that, before I come to England, full payment has been made of all the debts which, according to old-established law, we owe to God, namely, plough-alms, and the tithe of animals born during the year, and the pence which we owe to St Peter at Rome, both from towns and villages, and, in the middle of August, the tithe of fruits, and at the feast of St Martin the first-fruits of the crops (called in English "ciricsceatt") which each one owes to the church of the parish in which he lives.

Now, therefore, I command and implore all my bishops and reeves of the kingdom, by the faith which you owe to God and to me, that you bring it about before I come to England that all the dues, which according to ancient law we owe to God, shall be paid in full, namely plough-alms and tithe of livestock born that same year, and the pence which we owe to St Peter at Rome, whether from the towns or the villages, and in the middle of August tithe of the fruits of the earth, and at the feast of St Martin the firstfruits of the grain (which are called “church-scot” in English) to the church of the parish where each man resides.
div.note: Cn 1020 8; II Eg 2.3; II Eg 3; II Eg 4; II Eg 2.2

note.label: reverts to
note.quote: the author of Cnut's 1027 letter (Lyfing of Tavistock and Crediton?) reverted to something like Æthelstan's payment deadline

div.note: Latin only (Cnut's letter of 1027, c. May; Latin translation c. 1070–1100, the Old English original is lost). Liebermann's text is from Florence of Worcester (ed. MGH SS XIII 126), compared with Ox (Oxford, Corpus 157 p. 329) and William of Malmesbury II 183; text in column T. Liebermann gives no German translation.

note.label: August
note.seg: Previous laws allowed a later date, the autumn equinox or All Saints

note.label: grain
note.seg: Liebermann considers this is merely a misunderstanding of the Old English word cyricsceat, with confusion of sceat with sæd “seed”. It should, however, be noted that church-scot was often paid in grain.
